title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This manuscript page belongs to Grothendieck's notes for his 1976 IHÉS lecture on the divided-power de Rham complex. It is written on the back of a reused typed sheet of SGA 7, exposé IX (monodromy pairing, Barsotti–Tate groups). That typed text is what appears as the 'neighbouring pages' and it has nothing to do with this page's mathematics.

The boxed definition reads
C_*^{DR}(X; S,S^+,γ_*,t) := colim_{σ∈Δ/X} A^{dim σ}(S,S^+,γ_*,t).

1. Setting. X is a simplicial set. (S,S^+,γ_*,t) is a parameter datum over a base ring k:
- S is a coalgebra (presumably cocommutative);
- S^+ is an 'augmentation' part carrying divided powers γ_*;
- t: S^+ → k is a linear form.

2. The building blocks. A^n(S,...) is a covariant functor on the simplex category Δ. It is the coalgebra-side (predual) model of divided-power 'polynomial differential forms' on the standard n-simplex, built from the datum.

3. The construction. C_*^{DR}(X;-) is the left Kan extension of A^• along the Yoneda embedding Δ → sSet. It is a graded, alternating (graded-cocommutative), differential k-coalgebra, with codifferential of degree −1. It has:
- an augmentation-type structure relating it to S;
- divided powers on the augmentation part C_+ = ker(augmentation).
Grothendieck notes that the comparison with S is not injective in general: for X = ∅ one gets C = 0.

4. Functoriality in X. C is covariant in X with all these structures. A marginal addition asserts that X ↦ C_*^{DR}(X;...) commutes with arbitrary colimits, 'or only filtered ones'. A deleted line had said the dual C^*_{DR} is contravariant in X.

5. Item e), base change. If the datum varies with the base, the base-changed datum (S^{k'},...) is obtained contravariantly. The cochain object is C^*_{DR}(X; datum^{k'}) = Hom(C_*^{DR}(X,-), k'), a divided-power cdga in the spirit of Sullivan's A_PL. C_* depends covariantly on the datum, which is visible from the colimit formula since A^* is covariant in the datum. As a function of the datum it commutes with arbitrary colimits. The item ends with the heading 'commutation with extension of the base ring'.

6. Item f), gradings. Suppose S is a graded coalgebra, S^+ is graded compatibly, the divided powers respect the grading, and t is homogeneous of degree δ. The page breaks off just as the induced structure on the base-changed data (S^{k'},...) is being stated. Presumably the conclusion is an extra (weight) grading on C_*^{DR}.

7. Purpose. The aim is a functorial, integral (characteristic-free) divided-power analogue of Sullivan's piecewise-polynomial de Rham forms on simplicial sets. Working on the coalgebra/chain side lets one take colimits without finiteness problems. The cochain algebra is then recovered by duality, with base change built in.
errors: The direction of the 'augmentation' is inconsistent on the page. It is first written as a map S → C_*^{DR}(X,-), then C_+ is defined as ker(augm. C → C_*^{DR}). The second may be a slip or a mis-transcription for the counit C_*^{DR} → (S or k).

Commutation with arbitrary colimits is automatic for a left Kan extension along Yoneda if colimits are taken in the category of plain dg coalgebras; X = ∅ then gives the initial object 0, consistent with the remark. Once the augmentation or co-unit structure relative to S is imposed, coproducts in that augmented category are no longer computed naively. Grothendieck's hedge 'ou seulement filtrantes' is therefore warranted. The page does not settle which statement holds.
The statement Hom(C_*,k') = C^*(X; datum^{k'}) implicitly requires finiteness or flatness hypotheses (e.g. A^n free of finite type) for Hom to commute with the base change. These are not stated here.

ideas.what: Divided-power polynomial de Rham forms on simplices assembled over Δ/X, giving a functorial integral analogue of Sullivan's A_PL
ideas.modern_name: Integral/divided-power Sullivan–de Rham forms (simplicial PD-de Rham complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational case, 1977); Cenkl–Porter (integral/tame de Rham theories, ca. 1981–83); later Mandell's E∞-cochains (2006) for integral homotopy types
ideas.where_published: The 1976 IHÉS lecture seems not to have been published; Pursuing Stacks discusses integral models of homotopy types but I am unsure it contains this construction

ideas.what: Working on the coalgebra (chain) side as a colimit over the simplex category, so that the construction commutes with colimits of simplicial sets and dualizes to the cochain cdga with base change
ideas.modern_name: Left Kan extension / nerve–realization adjunction to PD dg coalgebras
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard Kan-extension formalism; the coalgebra viewpoint in rational homotopy is due to Quillen (1969)

ideas.what: A parametrized family of 'interval data' (S,S^+,γ,t), with covariance in the datum and an optional grading where t has degree δ
ideas.modern_name: Choice of interval or coefficient object for simplicial forms; weight-graded variant

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a general, parameter-dependent divided-power de Rham coalgebra functor on simplicial sets. It is meant to be functorial in the coefficient datum, compatible with base change and colimits, and with an optional weight grading (t of degree δ). This is an early program for integral models of homotopy types via divided-power differential forms. Neither this general formalism nor the 1976 lecture appears to have been written up.
missed.quote: C_*^{DR}(X;S,S^+,γ_*,t) def= lim_{σ∈Δ/X} A^{dimσ}(S,S^+,γ_*,t) ... f) Supposons que la coalgèbre S soit graduée ... t: S^+→k homog. de degré δ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic models of homotopy types are active topics: Mandell's theorem, Toën's affine stacks, and Horel and others on integral models. A flexible PD-de Rham model with a variable interval datum and a weight grading could relate to that work and to crystalline/PD analogues. Priority-wise, the construction predates or parallels Cenkl–Porter.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a definitional page from a little-known 1976 lecture anticipating integral divided-power analogues of Sullivan forms. It is a historically interesting early instance, but the formal steps shown here (Kan extension, functoriality, base change) are routine. The deeper content presumably lies elsewhere in the notes.
transcription_corrections: The neighbouring 'pages' (SGA 7 IX, p.117–118 typed) are the typed text on the reverse/background of the reused paper, not mathematically related to this manuscript page.
Marginal note at left reads roughly: 'X ↦ C_*^{DR}(X;...) commute aux lim. ind. quelconques (ou seulement filtrantes...)'. It is placed as a marginal insertion, not in the main text line.
The line '(pas une injectif ... si X=∅ C_*^{DR}(X,-)=0 ...)' should read roughly '(pas injectif: p. ex. si X=∅, C_*^{DR}(X,-)=0 ...)'.
The last line likely ends with a superscript '(S^{k'}/S)^{k'}' style datum; the base-change notation is partly illegible.
